sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Production occasionally serves an old value after a cache key was invalidated.
The visible test reproduces one ordering, but the problem is intermittent and its
root cause is unknown. Investigate `src/`, fix the race, and check the related
failure and mutation paths against the contract in `src/cache.js`. Preserve the
CommonJS named export `createCache`, its API, and concurrent load deduplication.
Do not add dependencies. The cache uses an injectable clock; do not introduce
real timers or sleeps.

Work only in the current directory. Do not modify `test/` or `package.json`.
Verify the fix with `node --test`.

arguments.command: find . -type f -not -path './node_modules/*' | head -50 && echo --- && cat package.json

content.text:
The bug is in `src/flight.js`: when a flight settles, it unconditionally does `pending.delete(key)` and `commit(value)` — even if the flight was detached by `invalidate`/`set`/`clear` and a newer flight or value has taken its place. So an obsolete load can (a) overwrite a fresher committed/set value with a stale one, and (b) delete a newer flight from the registry. A second latent issue: rejected flights are never removed from `pending`, so a later `get` joins the settled rejection forever instead of being able to retry.

Fix: give each flight an identity (its own promise) and only detach/commit when it is still the registered flight; rejections detach but never commit.

content.text:
Done. The race was in `src/flight.js`, fixed with a single change; `src/cache.js` and `src/clock.js` needed no modifications.

## Root cause

When a flight settled, `run()` **unconditionally** executed `pending.delete(key)` and `commit(value)`, regardless of whether the flight had been detached by `invalidate`/`set`/`clear` in the meantime. Because the stale value was only resurrected when an old flight settled *after* a barrier but *before/after* a newer flight in particular interleavings, the failure appeared intermittent. Two contract violations resulted:

1. **Stale resurrection** — an obsolete flight committed its value over a fresher `set`/loaded value (the visible test's ordering).
2. **Flight detachment** — an obsolete flight's `pending.delete(key)` removed a *newer* flight from the registry, breaking deduplication and barrier semantics ("Repeated invalidations are separate barriers").

A third latent bug on the failure path: the promise chain had no rejection handler, so a rejected flight was never removed from `pending` — every subsequent `get` joined the permanently-settled rejection instead of retrying, violating "Rejected loads are never cached… a subsequent get may retry."

## Fix

Each flight now uses its own promise as an identity token. On settle it acts only if it is still the registered flight for its key:

- **Fulfill:** commit + unregister only when still current — obsolete flights deliver their value to original waiters but never store or detach newer flights.
- **Reject:** unregister only when still current, rethrow the original reason unchanged — rejections are never committed, all waiters share the same reason, and retries work.

## Verification

`node --test` passes, plus a scratch script (not added to `test/`) confirmed: invalidate/set/clear barriers, `set` winning over in-flight loads, expired `set` value triggering a fresh load rather than joining the detached one, rejection fan-out and retry, sync throws and non-Error reasons, re-entrant `invalidate`/`set`/self-read inside `load`, `ttlMs: 0` dedup semantics, TTL starting at commit with exact `now() >= deadline` expiry, `size` ignoring flights, `undefined` returns from mutators, and constructor validation. No dependencies, timers, or API changes; concurrent-load deduplication is preserved.
